result.summary: All four gate questions clear. One robustness gap filed as ISS-0831 (non-blocking). Design doc stale on parser format — noted for DOC-UPDATER, not a gate condition.

findings.detail: System.cmd("mix", ["xref", "graph", "--format", "plain"]) from a Mix.Task is the standard approach for shelling out to a built-in Mix command from another task. No OTP process, no supervision entry, no ETS — correct for a pure-tooling check that runs at build time. classify_edge/2 is properly stateless and separated from the I/O in run/1. No gen_statem or GenServer misuse — this isn't a state machine at all, which is correct.
No processes started, no supervised trees touched, no singleton, no unsupervised spawn. The task is pure function composition + one System.cmd call + one IO.puts/Mix.raise. Nothing to supervise.

Commit touches exactly the three files specified by the requirement (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_boundaries.ex, test/mix/tasks/letflow.check_boundaries_test.exs, mix.exs) plus the ELIXIR-DEV handoff artefact. The mix.exs change is exactly one alias step ("letflow.check_boundaries") inserted between "compile --warnings-as-errors" and "letflow.check.test", with an explanatory comment. deps[] and mix.lock are unchanged. No new abstractions, no behaviour or macro plumbing introduced ahead of need.

D3 specifies exactly two violation classes: (1) any file outside lib/letflow/modules/<id>/ references a file inside one, except lib/letflow/modules/catalog.ex; (2) a file in lib/letflow/modules/a/ references lib/letflow/modules/b/ when b is not in a's depends_on. The implementation decomposes these into Rules 0–5 in first-match order, which is equivalent: Rule 0 (target not in module subdir → OK) and Rule 1 (catalog.ex sanctioned importer) are the explicit exception from D3; Rules 2–3 (intra-module, authorized cross-module) are the non-violation cases implied by D3's second class; Rule 4 is D3's second violation class; Rule 5 is D3's first violation class. No deviation from D3 intent, no extra rule invented. The sanctioned-importer exception is encoded as an exact path equality check on "lib/letflow/modules/catalog.ex", matching D3's literal wording.

classify_edge/2 has one test per case from design §2.3 (all 7 cases including the intra-module non-violation). All use synthetic edges — no live xref output, no DB, no process. The reason-string tests (two) assert that violation messages name the module IDs and the catalog.ex exception, giving regression protection on message format. parse_xref_output/1 covers blank input, both tree-char prefixes (|-- and `--), space-indented fallback, annotation stripping (compile/runtime), multi-source/multi-target, and orphan-target graceful skip. build_depends_on_map/1 covered for empty and populated cases. System test (AC2) uses System.cmd against the real project tree and asserts exit 0 + "OK" substring. T-ALIAS-WIRED and T-ALIAS-SLOT tests assert ordering invariant. No test creates a temp file that isn't cleaned up — the AC3 probe was an ELIXIR-DEV procedure, not a persisted test, consistent with design §5.4.

findings.area: Parser format deviation (design artefact vs. actual xref output)
findings.detail: The design artefact (req405-check-boundaries.md §1.2) describes target lines as 'Lines indented by one or more spaces'. The actual mix xref graph --format plain emits tree characters (|-- and `--) as target-line prefixes, not plain spaces. ELIXIR-DEV caught and handled this during implementation — the parser handles both tree-char and space-indented forms. The code's own @moduledoc and parse_xref_output/1 @doc correctly describe the actual format. The ELIXIR-DEV handoff records the deviation. Not a D3 consistency issue; the boundary classification logic is unaffected. Routing to DOC-UPDATER to correct §1.2 of the design artefact.

Letflow.Modules.Catalog.all_manifests/0 calls entry_modules/0 which returns @modules, a module attribute baked at compile time via Application.compile_env(:letflow, :modules, []). No runtime Application.get_env call, no ETS, no process lookup. Calling this from a Mix.Task that does not start the OTP application is safe and correct. This is confirmed by catalog.ex's own @moduledoc ('Read once at compile time via Application.compile_env/3 (not Application.get_env/3)') and by the design artefact §1.4 ('No app.start requirement needed — its data is compile_env-baked').

run/1 binds the System.cmd result as {output, _exit_code}, discarding the exit code. If mix xref itself exits non-zero (e.g., a transient xref failure, an unexpected internal error), the task will silently parse empty or error output, find 0 edges, and print 'OK -- 0 edges checked, 0 violations' — a false negative. In normal use the alias runs after compile --warnings-as-errors, so a broken compile is already caught before xref runs. The risk is low but the silent-OK shape is dangerous for a gate task. Filed as ISS-0831 (robustness, non-blocking) per the review procedure.
